newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Firmer in line with crude gains.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Firmer in line with crude gains.

text.p: The Singapore high sulphur fuel oil market traded firmer on Wednesday in line with gains in crude values, traders said.
September Brent crude last traded up 16 cents to $18.75 per barrel on the International Petroleum Exchnage after putting on 18 cents overnight.
Fuel oil swaps were actively traded, with both August and September up to $100.75/$101.75 from Tuesday's $99.25/$99.75.
A 180-cst grade cargo exchanged hands between two local traders at $101.75 per tonne while bids for the 380-cst grades moved up to $98.75 from $96 earlier.
"The fuel oil gains are mainly following the crude market," said one trader, noting American Pertroleum Institute stocks data which showed a crude shortfall of 9.7 million barrels.
Traders said prices could remain firm on Thursday.
"The fuel oil market will follow the crude market, which looks likely to maintain the gains," said another trader.
State-owned Petroleum Authority of Thailand (PTT) is expected to award a tender on Thursday to buy 80,000 tonnes of 180-cst fuel oil for September 1-10 delivery.
The tender, which seeks 6,000 tonnes of 1.0-percent sulphur and 74,000 tonnes of 2.0-percent fuel oil.
The low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) market was quiet as Indonesia would allocate more supplies in August than in July, traders said.
Indonesia's state oil company Pertamina allocated a total of 2.7 million barrels of LSWR for August lifting, traders said.
The allocation compared with the initial allocation of 2.3 million barrels in July, with additional 300,000 barrels rolled over from June.
